chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn 'Amr al-Rummani, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever recites Surah al-Mursalat, God will establish affection between him and Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
And whoever recites Surah al-Naba (Amma Yatasaa'aloon), if he recites it daily for a year, a year will not pass before he visits the Sacred House of Allah, if God wills.
And whoever recites Surah al-Naziat, he will not die except in a cheerful state, nor will God raise him except in a cheerful state, nor will He admit him to Paradise except in a cheerful state.

key_terms.الْمُرْسَلَاتِ: Surah al-Mursalat (The Emissaries), the 77th chapter of the Quran.
key_terms.بَيْتَ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامَ: The Sacred House of Allah (Kaaba in Mecca).
key_terms.رَيِّاناً: Cheerful, hearty, or in a state of joy/pleasure.
key_terms.عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ: The opening phrase of Surah al-Naba (The Great News), the 78th chapter.
key_terms.وَ النَّازِعَاتِ: Surah al-Naziat (Those who drag forth), the 79th chapter.

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of reciting Surah Mursalat, Naba, and Naziat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the eschatological benefits of specific Surahs, linking Surah al-Mursalat to spiritual affinity with the Prophet, Surah al-Naba to the fulfillment of Hajj, and Surah al-Naziat to a blessed state of 'Rayyan' (cheerfulness) at death and resurrection. The term 'Rayyan' specifically evokes the gate of Paradise reserved for those who fasted, suggesting a connection between recitation and the spiritual discipline of fasting. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of Quranic recitation in shaping one's final moments and afterlife status.
